cands.name: Seth Harp
cands.bio: Democratic nominee. Gainesville civics teacher at Lincoln Middle School; radio and media manager for 20+ years (WKZO Kalamazoo talk host from age 23, later program/operations/station manager; ESPN Gainesville operations manager; UF journalism adjunct). Won the Democratic primary with 45.2%. Never held elected office. Not the journalist of the same name.
cands.local_ties: Lives in Gainesville; moved to Florida more than a decade ago. Bachelor's degree from Western Michigan University (News4JAX guide).

record.text: Platform ('13 Stripes of Strength'): Social Security stabilization, housing/child-care/student-debt measures, universal health care, protecting water, ending tax loopholes (self-described, News4JAX voter guide).
Won the Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary: Harp 20,671 (45.2%), Tom Wells 15,447 (33.8%), Troy Albers 5,188 (11.3%), George Hubac 4,458 (9.7%) (per Wikipedia).

endorsements.text: Florida LGBTQ+ Democratic Caucus (listed on Blue Voter Guide; not otherwise verified).

cands.gaps: Sources differ on teaching grade (6th vs 7th). A Cammack strategist criticized him in Sept 2025 (Floridian Press) - not opened. No fundraising or outside-money details. Photo is from his own site; identity matches the file name 'Sethteaching' but was not independently confirmed.

cands.name: Mike Klein
cands.bio: Independent (no party affiliation), 58. West Point graduate (engineering and international relations), Army combat veteran, MBA-level degree from the University of South Carolina. Chairman of Warrior Centric Health. Over three decades supporting campaigns and causes, including managing a presidential campaign (Dennis Kucinich's, per the Florida Alligator). Never held elected office.
cands.local_ties: Gainesville resident; launched his campaign July 4, 2026 at Bo Diddley Plaza in Gainesville.

record.text: Platform: 'Main Street Cost of Living Plan,' localizing food/energy/manufacturing, rural and veterans' health care, workforce housing; says he takes no corporate PAC money (candidate questionnaire, News4JAX).
Argues an independent could push reform in a divided House; says life is 'not affordable for normal people anymore' (The Capitolist).

endorsements.text: Dennis Kucinich (former Ohio congressman, his former campaign manager relationship noted by the Florida Alligator), at a Sept 24, 2026 UF forum on war and peace.
Forward Party, Independent Veterans of America and Track AIPAC (listed on the Wikipedia 2026 district page; sources not opened).

cands.gaps: Social handles not verified individually. No fundraising/outside-money details. Not a Marine (an early prompt said 'veteran'; sources say West Point graduate and Army veteran).

cands.name: Kat Cammack
cands.bio: Republican, born 1988 in Denver and raised on a cattle ranch. Deputy chief of staff to Rep. Ted Yoho 2013-2019; won the 3rd district seat in 2020 and is seeking a fourth term. Chairs the Republican Women's Caucus and co-chairs the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus.
cands.local_ties: Returned to Florida in 2019; district covers North Central Florida (Gainesville/Alachua, Lake City and Suwannee area to Marion/Ocala).

record.text: 119th Congress committees: Agriculture (Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development) and Energy and Commerce (Commerce, Manufacturing and Trade; Communications and Technology; Health).
Chair, Republican Women's Caucus (2025-present); chair of the Congressional Women's Caucus 2023-2025; co-chair of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus.
Did not respond to News4JAX's 2026 candidate questionnaire; faced no primary challenger.

controversies.text: January 2023: claimed without evidence that Democrats were drinking alcohol and eating popcorn during the Speaker vote (per Wikipedia).
Spring 2022: baby-formula images shown on Fox News were of milk products for children over one; Sean Hannity acknowledged the error (per Wikipedia).

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (Florida Politics, Oct 16, 2025; page paywalled, not opened). AIPAC, Maggie's List and Log Cabin Republicans are listed on the Wikipedia 2026 district page.

cands.gaps: Photo skipped per brief. Bills she sponsored not verified (Wikipedia lists only cosponsored). No verified outside-spending or donor data (an AFP spending item seen only in a search summary was omitted). Social handles not verified.

votes.what: Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.
Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.
